ai.description: *Indirana sarojamma* is a small frog (25–35 mm) with a brown, granular dorsum and a distinct dark lateral band. It features a pointed snout and elongated, slender digits with small terminal discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana sarojamma* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored lateral band that extends from the snout through the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Indirana sarojamma* inhabits the leaf litter of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Sarojamma's leaping frogs are primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the mossy, wet rocks of their stream-side habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana sarojamma* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–300 eggs on wet rocks near streams, where tadpoles develop semi-terrestrially in thin water films.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana sarojamma* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Indirana sarojamma* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps emitted from rocky, stream-side habitats in the Western Ghats.
